title: Intonational Invariance under Changes in Pitch Range and Length
abstract: Chapter 10 of Language Sound Structure. Two speech production experiments varying overall pitch range, phrase order, and list length establish that a speaker's lowest F0 values are nearly invariant while peaks scale freely, that phrase-final pitch accents undergo a separate multiplicative lowering, and that downstep is a constant-ratio decay above a reference line that rises with pitch range. The resulting model of F0 implementation computes each target from the immediately preceding one, requires no whole-phrase preplanning, and reinterprets the phenomena collectively called declination as the joint result of local downstep, final lowering, and pitch-range choice. Fitted per-speaker constants and comparisons against additive log models, Fujisaki's command-response model, and configurational rise-fall theories are reported.
container_title: Language Sound Structure: Studies in Phonology Presented to Morris Halle by His Teacher and Students
